17.1 What this tab is for #

The View+Edit tab shows the files that PTXprint uses and creates. You can edit two of them here: the front matter (the pages before the Scripture text, such as the title page and the table of contents) and the Adj List (the list of paragraph adjustments).

Come here to:

  • create or change the front matter (title page, copyright page, contents page, preface);
  • make a paragraph one line longer or shorter so that a page fits better;
  • see the text exactly as PTXprint sent it to the typesetting program;
  • read the log of the last print run when something went wrong.

The tab is only shown in the Regular and Full views. In the Basic view PTXprint still uses the front matter and Adj List that you made before.

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents17.2 The sub-tabs: which files you may edit →

17.2 The sub-tabs: which files you may edit #

Each small tab (sub-tab) along the top shows one file.

Sub-tab What it shows Can you edit it here?
Front Matter The front matter for this configuration (title page, copyright page, contents, and so on). Yes. This is the main place to edit front matter.
Adj List A table of paragraph adjustments for the Book in Focus. Yes. You can change values in the table.
Final SFM The text of one book after PTXprint has applied all its changes, as it was sent to the typesetter. No – look only. It is created again each time you print.
.tex file The control file that PTXprint wrote for the last print run. No – look only.
XeTeX Log The log (report) of the last print run. No – look only.
Settings (up to three) Other settings files that you chose to open from the Advanced tab. Advanced users only – see the Advanced tab chapter.

Important: Make changes to the Scripture text in Paratext, not on the Final SFM sub-tab. That file is replaced every time you print.

The .tex file and XeTeX Log are useful when you ask for help. A supporter may ask you to look for an error message in the XeTeX Log. You do not need to understand these files to use PTXprint.

Very long log files are cut short on the screen. Click View/Edit... to see the whole file in your computer's text editor.

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 17.1 What this tab is for17.3 The buttons at the top of the tab →

17.3 The buttons at the top of the tab #

The buttons change with the open sub-tab. Buttons that do not apply are greyed out.

  • Refresh reloads the file from the disk. Unsaved changes are lost.
  • Book in Focus chooses which book is shown (only on Adj List and Final SFM).
  • Generate creates new content for the open sub-tab (see below).
  • View/Edit... opens the file in your computer's own text editor. On the look-only sub-tabs it is called View Only....
  • Edit Variables... (only on Front Matter) takes you to the variables table on the Peripherals tab.
  • The information button (only active on Front Matter) lists the special codes when you hold the mouse over it.
  • Autosave decides whether changes are saved without asking.
  • The slider changes the size of the text in the editing area.

Saving your changes #

When you change the text on an editable sub-tab, the sub-tab name turns red: there are unsaved changes. PTXprint saves them:

  • when you click outside the text area (without asking if Autosave is ticked, otherwise after asking);
  • when you click Print while an editable sub-tab is open.

To throw away your changes, click Refresh (or press F5) before you click elsewhere.

If the configuration is locked (see the Basic tab), you cannot generate or save front matter, and Autosave is turned off.

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 17.2 The sub-tabs: which files you may edit17.4 The Generate button →

17.4 The Generate button #

Generate does a different job on each sub-tab:

  • Front Matter – opens the Generate Front Matter dialog, to start the front matter from a template.
  • Adj List – makes a new adjustment list for the books you are printing (see The Adj List below).
  • Final SFM – makes the Final SFM file again for the Book in Focus.

On the other sub-tabs Generate is greyed out.

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 17.3 The buttons at the top of the tab17.5 The Generate Front Matter dialog →

17.5 The Generate Front Matter dialog #

Click Generate on the Front Matter sub-tab and choose one of four starting points:

  • BASIC – title page, copyright and licence page, table of contents. A good start for most projects.
  • ADVANCED – more sections, with sample English text that you must translate or delete.
  • DIGLOT – a fuller template for diglot or polyglot publications (two or more languages).
  • PARATEXT – a copy of the FRT (front matter) book from your Paratext project.

See the control notes below for details of each.

Warning: OK replaces all of the current front matter. Your earlier changes are lost. If you have worked on your front matter, click Cancel.

After OK, PTXprint also finds any new variables (\zvar|...\* codes) in the new front matter and adds them to the variables table on the Peripherals tab.

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 17.4 The Generate button17.6 The front matter and its special codes (advanced) →

17.6 The front matter and its special codes (advanced) #

The front matter uses USFM markers, as in Paratext (for example \mt1 for a main title and \pc for a centred paragraph). PTXprint also understands extra codes that start with \z, often called z-codes. Hold the mouse over the information button for a short list.

Each configuration has its own front matter. If you make a new configuration, check its front matter too.

Sections (periph) #

The front matter is divided into sections. Each section starts with a line such as:

\periph Title Page|id="title"

Each section normally starts on a new page.

If you used the Cover Wizard (on the Peripherals tab), the cover sections are at the end of the front matter, after the line \rem ============= Cover Page Settings =============. The wizard replaces these sections each time you click Finish. If you change them here, the wizard asks to delete the old cover settings the next time you open it.

Text from other settings #

  • \zcopyright – the copyright statement from the Basic tab.
  • \zlicense – the licence statement from the Basic tab. (Type it with an s.)
  • \zimagecopyrights – a list of the pictures used, with their pages and copyright credits. Add a language code at the end for another language, for example \zimagecopyrightsfr for French. The list is only correct after you print twice, because PTXprint first needs to find the page of each picture.

Put these codes after a paragraph marker, for example: \pc \zcopyright

Variables #

\zvar|maintitle\* is a variable: a place-holder for a piece of text. When you print, PTXprint replaces it with the value from the variables table on the Peripherals tab. You can make up your own names, for example \zvar|printedby\*. The values are saved with the configuration, so two configurations can use the same front matter with different titles.

\zvar|toctitle\* is special. It uses the text in the Table of contents title box on the Peripherals tab.

Space and blank lines #

  • \zbl|3\* – inserts 3 blank lines.
  • \zgap|1.5in\* – inserts a space of the given height (for example 1.5in, 20mm, 30pt).

Page numbers #

  • \nopagenums – do not print page numbers from here on.
  • \dopagenums – print page numbers again.
  • \resetpagenums -1 – start the page numbers again. A negative number gives Roman numerals (i, ii, iii...).

Table of contents #

\ztoc|main\* puts the table of contents here. Instead of main you can use: pre (books before the Scripture text), ot (Old Testament only), heb (Old Testament in Hebrew order), dc (Deuterocanon only), nt (New Testament only), post (books after Revelation, such as a glossary), or sorta, sortb, sortc (alphabetical lists sorted by \toc1, \toc2 or \toc3). Also tick Table of Contents on the Peripherals tab.

Code Snippets buttons #

On the Front Matter sub-tab, the buttons under Code Snippets list ready-made codes in groups (for example Periph+Var, Insert, ISBN+QR, Contents, Pages, Diglot). Put the cursor where you want the code, click a group button, then choose an item. Hold the mouse over an item to see what it does. The Settings sub-tabs have their own snippet buttons for the type of file that is open.

Keyboard shortcuts in the front matter editor #

  • Ctrl+0 or Ctrl+comma – turn the current line into a comment (\rem), or back again.
  • Ctrl+D – copy (duplicate) the current line.
  • Ctrl+L – delete the current line.
  • Ctrl+Up / Ctrl+Down – move the current line up or down.
  • Ctrl+minus / Ctrl+equals – make the text in the editor smaller or larger.
  • Alt+X – show the Unicode values of the selected characters in the status bar.
↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 17.5 The Generate Front Matter dialog17.7 The Adj List (adjustment list) →

17.7 The Adj List (adjustment list) #

Sometimes a page ends badly: for example, one line of a paragraph is alone at the top of the next page, or the two columns do not end at the same height. You can often fix this by asking PTXprint to set one paragraph a little tighter (one line less) or looser (one line more).

The Adj List is the list of these requests. Each row is one paragraph. The columns are:

  • Book and C.V – the book, chapter and verse where the paragraph is.
  • Para – which paragraph: 1 is the paragraph that contains the verse, 2 is the next one, and so on. This lets you adjust, for example, the paragraph after a heading.
  • Stretch – the change. +1 asks for one line more, -1 for one line less. After Generate, you also see values such as +0, -0 or +-0. These mean "no change yet", and show whether the paragraph can grow (+) or shrink (-).
  • Marker – the paragraph marker (for example p or q1).
  • Expand – how much the letters are spread out or squeezed, in percent. 100 is normal.
  • Parameters and Comment – extra information.

Click a cell to change its value. To delete rows, select them and press the Delete key, or right-click and choose Delete Row(s).

For a diglot, the book code has an L or R after it (for example MATL and MATR) to show the side.

Generate on the Adj List sub-tab prints the books three times in the background (normal, tight, loose) to learn which paragraphs can shrink or grow. This can take some time. If an Adj List already exists, PTXprint asks whether to replace it (Yes), merge the new information into it (No – the safe choice), or do nothing (Cancel).

It is usually easier to adjust from the PDF Preview window: right-click a paragraph and choose to shrink or expand it. PTXprint writes those changes into this same Adj List.

Do paragraph adjustments last. Any change to fonts, margins, pictures or other layout settings moves the text, and your adjustments may then be wrong.

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 17.6 The front matter and its special codes (advanced)17.8 Common tasks →

17.8 Common tasks #

Create front matter for the first time #

  1. On the Peripherals tab, tick Local Front Matter. If there is no front matter yet, PTXprint makes a BASIC one for you.
  2. On the View+Edit tab, click the Front Matter sub-tab.
  3. For a different template, click Generate, choose BASIC, ADVANCED, DIGLOT or PARATEXT, and click OK.
  4. Click Edit Variables... and type the values (title, subtitle and so on) in the Value column.
  5. Click Print. If the front matter has a table of contents or picture credits, click Print again.

Change the text on the title page #

  1. On the View+Edit tab, click the Front Matter sub-tab.
  2. If the line says \mt1 \zvar|maintitle\*, the title comes from a variable. Click Edit Variables... and change the value of maintitle.
  3. If the line contains normal text, change the text directly in the editor.
  4. Click outside the text area to save, then click Print.

Add a copyright page with picture credits #

  1. Open the Front Matter sub-tab.

  2. Put the cursor where the copyright information should go.

  3. Type these lines (or use the Insert snippet button):

     \pc \zcopyright
 \pc \zlicense
 \pc \zimagecopyrights

  4. Click Print twice.

Make a paragraph one line shorter or longer #

  1. Finish all other layout settings first.
  2. Easiest: in the PDF Preview window, right-click the paragraph to shrink or expand it.
  3. Or: on the Adj List sub-tab, choose the Book in Focus, find the paragraph and type -1 or +1 in the Stretch column.
  4. Click Print and check the result.

See what text PTXprint actually typeset #

  1. Click Print once, so the file exists.
  2. On the View+Edit tab, click the Final SFM sub-tab.
  3. Choose the book in Book in Focus.
  4. Read the text. Do not edit it – make corrections in Paratext.

Look at the log after a failed print #

  1. Click the XeTeX Log sub-tab.
  2. Scroll to the end. Error messages usually start with !.
  3. If the log is cut short, click View Only... to open the whole file.
↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 17.7 The Adj List (adjustment list)17.9 Common problems →

17.9 Common problems #

My changes to the front matter disappeared. You probably clicked Generate and then OK, which replaces the whole front matter. Or you clicked Refresh, or answered "No" to "Save changes?". There is no undo. Keep a copy of important text before you generate a new template.

The front matter does not appear in the PDF. Tick Local Front Matter on the Peripherals tab.

A variable prints as "". The variable has no value yet. Type one in the variables table on the Peripherals tab.

The licence statement does not print. Check that the code is spelled \zlicense (with an s).

The table of contents or the picture credits are empty or wrong. PTXprint needs a first print run to find the page numbers. Click Print again.

The View+Edit tab is missing. You are using the Basic or Mini view. Change the view level to Regular or Full in the main menu.

The Generate button is greyed out. It does not work on the .tex file, XeTeX Log and Settings sub-tabs. On the Front Matter sub-tab, it is also greyed out when the configuration is locked.

"The Book in focus is not within scope". You clicked Generate on the Adj List sub-tab, but the Book in Focus is not in the list of books to print. Choose a book that you are printing, or add the book on the Basic tab.

Paragraph adjustments no longer do what I expected. The layout has changed since you made them (for example a new font size or new pictures). Check the adjustments again, or generate a new Adj List.

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 17.8 Common tasks17.10 Settings reference →

17.10 Settings reference #

Generate Front Matter (dialog) #

OK #

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

Replaces the current front matter with the chosen template. Everything you typed before is lost.

Cancel #

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

Closes the dialog and keeps your front matter. Click this if you are not sure.

Generate Front Matter #

BASIC: Front matter contains just a few essentials with publication information #

Radio button · shown in: Regular and Full views
Also: Generate front matter: BASIC (just the essentials)

This option will create a simple verso page containing essential copyright and licensing information followed by a table of contents.

Contains a title page, a publication data page (copyright, licence and picture credits) and a table of contents. The titles come from variables such as maintitle and subtitle, so you only need to fill in the variables table on the Peripherals tab. A good choice for most first-time users.

ADVANCED: template contains several sections (some of which require editing before use) #

Radio button · shown in: Regular and Full views
Also: Generate front matter: ADVANCED (requires editing)

This option will create an extensive template with multiple sections (each of which will start on a new page in the final publication). You will need to edit the sample text provided so that it communicates in the required language(s). You can also remove unwanted sections if they are inappropriate for this publication. Note: In order to make this template generic for several different publications in this project, you are encouraged to use \zvar|variables\* which will be replaced with publication-specific info when printed. For example:
\mt1 \zvar|maintitle\*
\mt2 \zvar|subtitle\*
\pc \zvar|maintitlefr\*
\pc \zvar|subtitlefr\*
\pc \zvar|languagename\*
\pc \zvar|copiesprinted\*

Contains title page, publication data, foreword, preface, table of contents and an alphabetical contents list. The foreword and preface have sample English text to replace or delete. It uses more variables (for example languagename, copiesprinted, printedby), which you fill in on the Peripherals tab.

Include sections for a separate cover page #

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views
Also: Generate front matter: Include sections for cover page

(Not yet implemented) Enable this option if you want to include the following sections (used for creating a cover page):
\periph Cover - detailing text and optional picture
\periph Spine - text for the spine of the cover

Does nothing yet, ticked or not. To make a cover, use Create Cover Page and the Cover Wizard... on the Peripherals tab.

DIGLOT: template for a Diglot or Polyglot publication (deliberately fuller — delete sections you do not need) #

Radio button · shown in: Regular and Full views
Also: Generate front matter: DIGLOT (for Diglot/Polyglot publications)

This option creates a DIGLOT / POLYGLOT front matter template designed for publications with two (or more) languages or scripts. It is deliberately more complete than the BASIC and ADVANCED templates because diglots are inherently complex: two (or more) texts, often two contents lists, two prefaces, sometimes two scripts and two writing directions. Delete the sections you do not need.

Like the ADVANCED template it uses \zvar|variables\* and
\zglot|L\* / \zglot|R\* markers for column-specific content, so it requires editing before use and is NOT suitable for use inside Paratext without prior modification.

If this option is disabled, the Diglot setting is not enabled for this configuration.

Has sections for both languages (for example two prefaces taken from each side's INT book) and also cover sections. Expect to delete several sections.

PARATEXT: Make a copy of the Project's FRT book (which may be edited to make use of \zvar|variables\*) #

Radio button · shown in: Regular and Full views
Also: Generate front matter: PARATEXT (make a local copy)

This option will create a COPY of the Paratext project's FRT book to be used exclusively by PTXprint. You can edit the front matter to make use of PTXprint-specific
\zvar|variables\* but note that none of these edits will be reflected in Paratext. In addition, if you edit the FRT book in Paratext, those changes will not be reflected here until you regenerate this (local) Front Matter.

If option is disabled, it is due to not having a FRT book in the Paratext project (so there is nothing to import).

After the copy, the two are separate: edits in Paratext do not appear here, and edits here do not go back to Paratext. Generate again to get the new Paratext version. Use this if your team already keeps good front matter in Paratext.

↑ Settings reference↑↑ Top of chapter

View+Edit #

Refresh #

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views
Also: Reload current file in view from saved version

Discard any changes that have been made and restore the contents of this file as it was when last saved.

Shortcut: F5

Use it to throw away unsaved changes, or after you changed the file in an outside editor. Greyed out on the look-only sub-tabs.

Book in Focus – Book in focus for editor (or viewer) #

Drop-down list · shown in: Regular and Full views
Choices: NONE

Choose any book (including those which are not currently in the list to be printed.)

Active only on the Adj List and Final SFM sub-tabs. Always greyed out when printing a module instead of books.

Generate #

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views
Also: Generate ... (context sensitive)

This button will (re-)generate content for Front Matter, AdjList(s) and Final SFM.

If you only want to (re-)generate an Adj List for a single book, then just select that book on the Basic tab. Otherwise it will (re-)generate a Pic/Adj list for each of the books listed for printing.

Shortcut: Ctrl-G

Opens the Generate Front Matter dialog on Front Matter, makes a new adjustment list on Adj List, or a fresh Final SFM file for the Book in Focus on Final SFM. An Adj List takes three background print runs, so it can be slow for large books.

View/Edit... #

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views
Also: View (or edit) file in external editor

You may view (and in some cases edit) the file in your system's text Editor.

Warning: If you edit settings in an external editor, be careful to save them (externally) and then click the refresh button (within PTXprint) before you hit Print. Otherwise you could lose changes that were made.

If nothing happens when you click here, it is probably because you have not associated the file type (.sfm, .piclist, .adjlist, .tex, .log, .sty etc.) with a text editor (such as Notepad or NP++).

Note that any changes to the Final SFM text get overwritten each time you hit Print. So any changes to the text or markers need to be made in Paratext.

Shortcut: Ctrl-E

Easier for long files or for searching. If you change a file there, save it in that editor, then click Refresh in PTXprint before you print. Otherwise PTXprint may save its own older copy over your changes.

Edit Variables... #

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views
Also: Edit peripheral variables

If you have used \zvar_variable names in the front matter template, these may be edited on the "Pub. Info" tab. Click this button to show that tab.

Before it switches tabs, it saves the front matter and adds any new \zvar names to the table, so you can type their values. Only shown on the Front Matter sub-tab.

Use the following codes to include special text in front mat... #

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views

Use the following codes to include special text in front matter:

\nopagenums - turn OFF page numbers
\dopagenums - turn ON page number
\resetpagenums # - where # is the page number (setting # to -1 gives roman numerals i,ii,iii,iv,v,...)

\pc \zcopyright - copyright statement from the Basic tab
\pc \zlicense - license statement from the Basic tab
\pc \zimagecopyrights - generated list of images with copyright attribution
\pc \zimagecopyrightsfr - as above, but localized (fr = French)

\zbl|3\* - inserts 3 blank lines
\zgap|1.5in\*

To include one or more table of contents:
\ztoc|\* Where can be replaced with:
main – primary, all-inclusive table of contents
pre – any book prior to scripture (FRT, INT)
ot – only Old Testament books are listed
heb - OT books sorted according to the Hebrew TaNaKh
dc – only Deutero Canonical books are listed
nt – only New Testament books are listed
post – books that occur after REV (GLO, BAK, TDX, NDX, XXA-G)
sorta – alphabetical (main) list sorted by \toc1
sortb – alphabetical (main) list sorted by \toc2
sortc – alphabetical (main) list sorted by \toc3

In addition to the above-mentioned codes, you may specify your own config-specific \zvar|variables\* as place-holders. Click on 'Edit Variables...' to assign values to these variables on the Peripherals tab. For example:
\mt1 \zvar|maintitle\*
\mt2 \zvar|subtitle\*

Only active on the Front Matter sub-tab. See "The front matter and its special codes" in this chapter for a fuller explanation.

Autosave #

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views

Save any changes made below without a confirmation check.

When not ticked, PTXprint asks "Save changes?" when you click outside the text area. Untick it if you often experiment and want to be asked. Greyed out on the look-only sub-tabs and when the configuration is locked.

Book in Focus – Adjust display font size #

Slider · shown in: Regular and Full views
Values: 8–20 (default 12)

Use this slider to adjust the size of the text on the View+Edit tab as well as in other locations that use a specialized font or script.

Keyboard Shortcuts:
Ctrl-Minus - shrink text size
Ctrl-Plus - grow text size

Affects only the screen (the editor and some other boxes that use the project font), not the PDF.

Adj List #

Label · shown in: Regular and Full views

To balance columns of text on a page it is possible to specify paragraphs adjustments (shrink or expand):

A Paragraph Adjust List needs to be in this format:
MRK 2.7 +1 (i.e. expand the para at Mark 2.7 by one line) MRK 3.20 -1 (i.e. shrink the para at Mark 3:20 by one line) %MARK 4.14 +1 (ignore this line - treat it as a comment) MRK 5.8 +2 (i.e. expand the para at Mark 5.8 by two lines) MRK 6.23 +1[2] (expand the paragraph AFTER the paragraph
which contains MRK 6.23 e.g. a heading.)

Diglot AdjList also need R or L to be specified after the book code and it is important that L comes before R for the same verse. MATL 3.4 +1 MATR 3.4 -1 MATR 3.11 +2

Keyboard Shortcuts:
Ctrl-1 - makes the current line +1
Ctrl-2 - makes the 2nd para of current line +1[2]
... etc ...
Ctrl-9 - makes the 9th para of current line +1[9]

Ctrl-I - shrink current line -1
Ctrl-Grave - ` same as above

Ctrl-0 - % Comment (or uncomment) the line [it toggles]
Ctrl-Comma - same as above

Ctrl-D - Duplicate the current line
Ctlr-L - deLete the current line
Ctrl-Up - move the current line up one line
Ctrl-Down - move the current line down one line

Note that adjusting paragraphs needs to be done right at the end when all other settings have been finalized. Otherwise you are likely to have to re-do it all again.

The table shows one row per paragraph for the Book in Focus. Type +1 or -1 in the Stretch column. See "The Adj List (adjustment list)" in this chapter for the columns.

Code Snippets #

Label · shown in: Regular and Full views

Use the buttons below to insert various code snippets as required.

The buttons appear on the Front Matter and Settings sub-tabs. Each opens a menu of ready-made codes; choose one to insert it at the cursor.

More... #

Link · shown in: Regular and Full views
Also: Link to deeper technical help

Online documentation on a structured list of code snippets which can be copied and pasted into the appropriate settings files.

Mostly for advanced users who work with the settings files on the Advanced tab.

18. Peripherals tab (front and back matter) #

In this chapter

18.1 What this tab is for #

The Peripherals tab controls everything printed around the Scripture text:

  • the front matter – the pages before the Scripture text, such as the title page, the copyright page and the table of contents;
  • the back matter – pages after the Scripture text, such as maps and the colophon;
  • a cover for the book;
  • ready-made PDF files to add at the front or at the back.

The words on the front matter pages are edited on the View+Edit tab. The special codes you can use there (\zcopyright, \ztoc, \zvar and others) are explained in the View+Edit tab chapter. This chapter explains the settings that turn these parts on and off, and the table of variables (values that PTXprint puts into the front matter, such as the main title).

View levels: In the Basic view this tab shows only Table of Contents, Local Front Matter and the variables table. Everything else needs the Regular or Full view. When one of the main options on this tab is on, the tab name is shown in a different colour.

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents18.2 Cover →

18.2 Cover #

PTXprint can make a cover: a back cover, a spine (the narrow back edge of a bound book) and a front cover, all on one wide page (the "cover spread"). The cover is saved in its own PDF file, with the name of the main PDF plus _cover. Printers usually print the cover on different paper, so they want a separate file.

  • Tick Create Cover Page to make a cover each time you print.
  • Click Cover Wizard... to design the cover step by step (see below).
  • The links Back Cover, Spine, Front Cover and Cover Spread open the matching style on the Styles tab. Each part of the cover is a sidebar (a box) with a background colour, background picture, border and other box settings. Use Cover Spread for things that go across the whole cover, for example one picture behind the back, spine and front.

The text on each part comes from special front matter sections (coverfront, coverspine, coverback, and coverwhole for the whole spread). So the cover needs Local Front Matter. If you untick Local Front Matter, PTXprint also unticks Create Cover Page and shows a message. If the front matter has no cover sections, no cover is made. The easiest way to create them is the Cover Wizard.

There is no separate Cover tab in this version. Use the Cover Wizard and the four style links.

The Cover Wizard #

The wizard window shows the steps on the left and a preview of the whole cover on the right. Use Next and Back to move between the steps.

If the configuration already has cover settings that the wizard did not make, or that were changed by hand afterwards, PTXprint first shows Existing cover settings found. The wizard cannot build on these. Delete and Continue deletes the old cover styles and sections and starts a new cover. Cancel (keep my settings) keeps them; the wizard does not open.

  1. Book and Spine Setup – type the approximate number of pages (PTXprint fills this in from the last PDF if it can). Choose whether the book has a spine (most books with fewer than about 80 pages have no spine text). If it has a spine, choose Paperback or Hardcover, and how to find the spine width: Automatic (from the paper weight in gsm or the paper thickness in µm) or Manual (type the width in mm). Ask your printer for the paper thickness if you can. Tick the right-to-left binding option for scripts such as Arabic or Hebrew, whose books open on the other side.
  2. Picture / decoration – choose where the main picture goes (none, whole cover, front only, front and spine, back only, back and spine, or separate front and back pictures). Choose the file, how it fits (stretch or crop), and its opacity. You can also add a decorative border to the front cover.
  3. Background – white, or a solid colour behind everything. (Gradient shading is not available yet.)
  4. Front cover text – type the title (required before you can go on). You can also add a subtitle, the language name and a picture. Each item has a position slider (higher or lower), a colour and a size.
  5. Spine text (only when the book has a spine) – choose what to show (title, subtitle, language name), its colour, size, direction and position. (The publisher name on the spine is not available yet.)
  6. Back cover – add a short text (a "blurb"), an ISBN barcode and a logo, and choose where they go.
  7. Review – check the summary and the preview, then click Finish.

When you click Finish, PTXprint:

  • ticks Local Front Matter if needed (the cover sections are kept in the front matter);
  • writes new cover sections at the end of the front matter, after the line \rem ============= Cover Page Settings =============. This replaces any earlier cover sections;
  • changes the cover styles (background, border, picture, title colours and sizes);
  • puts the title, subtitle, language name and ISBN into the variables maintitle, subtitle, languagename and isbn in the variables table on this tab;
  • saves your wizard answers with the configuration, so you can open the wizard later and make changes.

Cancel (or closing the window) changes nothing, and your answers go back to what they were when you opened the wizard.

If the publication is printed from the Publications tab, PTXprint works out the spine width from the page count of each publication (see the Publications tab chapter).

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 18.1 What this tab is for18.3 Front Matter PDF(s) and Back Matter PDF(s) →

18.3 Front Matter PDF(s) and Back Matter PDF(s) #

Use these when part of the book already exists as a PDF file, for example a title page made in another program, or maps or an index made elsewhere.

  • Tick Front Matter PDF(s) and click Select... to choose PDF files that go before the Scripture text.
  • Tick Back Matter PDF(s) and click Select... to choose PDF files that go after it.

The chosen file names are shown next to the button. Hold the mouse over Select... to see the full paths. Several files are added in the alphabetical order of their file names (not the order you clicked them). For a different order, name the files for example 01-title.pdf, 02-preface.pdf. The PDF pages must have the same page size as your publication.

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 18.2 Cover18.4 Table of Contents →

18.4 Table of Contents #

Tick Table of Contents to make a list of the books with their page numbers. It is useful when you print several books.

  • Title – the heading, for example "Contents" in your language.
  • Use \toc1 / \toc2 / \toc3 – each book in Paratext has up to three names: \toc1 (long name), \toc2 (short name) and \toc3 (abbreviation). Each ticked name becomes one column. At least one must be ticked.
  • Leaders – dots or a line between the book name and the page number.

Where does it appear?

  • Without Local Front Matter, PTXprint makes its own contents page with your title before the Scripture text.
  • With Local Front Matter, it appears where the front matter has \ztoc|main\* (see the View+Edit tab chapter). The BASIC front matter template already has this code.

The page numbers are only known after typesetting, so PTXprint typesets more than once when you click Print. With Quick Run ticked it typesets only once; the status line then says "Rerun to fix: table of contents", and you must click Print again.

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 18.3 Front Matter PDF(s) and Back Matter PDF(s)18.5 Local Front Matter →

18.5 Local Front Matter #

PTXprint does not print your Paratext project's FRT (front matter) book directly. It keeps its own copy for each configuration, which you change on the View+Edit tab. Tick Local Front Matter to print it. The first time, PTXprint makes a simple front matter (title page, copyright page and table of contents) if there is none yet.

  • Edit... opens the Front Matter sub-tab of the View+Edit tab.
  • Force Page Break at each Periph – each front matter section (title page, copyright page, preface …) starts on a new page.
  • Suppress Blank Page Before Scripture Text – stops the blank page PTXprint adds so that the Scripture text starts on a right-hand page.
  • Use Peripheral Introductory Sections – see below.

Note: Ticking Local Front Matter unticks Colophon at End of Publication, because most front matter already has a copyright page. Unticking it ticks the colophon again (and turns off the cover). Only your own click on Local Front Matter does this; opening a configuration or PTXprint updating the front matter does not change the colophon. Check both settings after you click one of them.

Use Peripheral Introductory Sections #

Some projects have an INT (introductions) book in Paratext, with sections such as an introduction to the Old Testament or to the Gospels. Each section starts with a \periph line that has an id. Tick Use Peripheral Introductory Sections to put each section in front of the first book of its group. The ids that PTXprint knows are:

id Placed before
intbible the first book of the Bible
intot the first Old Testament book
intpent the first book of the Pentateuch (GEN–DEU)
inthistory the first history book (JOS–EST)
intpoetry the first poetry book (JOB–SNG)
intprophesy the first book of the prophets (ISA–MAL)
intdc the first Deuterocanon book
intnt the first New Testament book
intgospels the first Gospel (MAT–JHN)
intepistles the first letter of Paul (ROM–PHM)
intletters the first of the other letters (HEB–REV)

A section is only printed when a book of its group is in the list of books to print. Force Page Break at each Periph also decides whether these sections start on a new page.

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 18.4 Table of Contents18.6 Maps →

18.6 Maps #

  • Add Maps... opens the Add Map dialog (explained in the Pictures tab chapter).
  • Include Maps adds the map book to the list of books to print.
  • Edit... shows the map book on the View+Edit tab.
↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 18.5 Local Front Matter18.7 Colophon at End of Publication →

18.7 Colophon at End of Publication #

A colophon is a short text at the very end of the book, for example the copyright, the licence and the picture credits. Tick Colophon at End of Publication to show the text box. The colophon is printed after the end of the last book.

  • Type the colophon in the Colophon Text box. You can use USFM markers such as \pc (centred paragraph) and the codes \zcopyright, \zlicense and \zimagecopyrights (see the View+Edit tab chapter).
  • The reset button below the box puts back the standard colophon.
  • Force Page Break Before Colophon puts the colophon on a new page.

The picture credits (\zimagecopyrights) need the page numbers of the pictures. Click Print a second time to get them right.

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 18.6 Maps18.8 Variables and Values →

18.8 Variables and Values #

This table lists the variables used in the front matter (and in the colophon and cover). A variable is a place-holder such as \zvar|maintitle\*. When you print, PTXprint puts the value from this table in its place. The values are saved with the configuration, so two configurations can use the same kind of front matter with different titles.

The table has three columns:

  • Pub (only in the Full view) – makes the variable a field of each publication on the Publications tab, so each publication can have its own value (for example its own title). maintitle and subtitle are always used there.
  • Name – the name of the variable. You cannot change it here.
  • Value – click to change it. Press Enter to keep the new value.

Buttons:

  • Rescan peripheral variables adds any \zvar|...\* codes in the front matter that are missing from the table.
  • Add adds a new variable.
  • Del deletes the selected variables.

The variable toctitle is special: it always uses the Title of the Table of Contents, so it is not in this table.

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 18.7 Colophon at End of Publication18.9 Common tasks →

18.9 Common tasks #

Add a title page and a copyright page #

  1. On the Basic tab, check the copyright and licence statements.
  2. On the Peripherals tab, tick Local Front Matter. PTXprint makes a simple front matter if there is none.
  3. In the Variables and Values table, click the value of maintitle and type the title. Do the same for subtitle and any other variables.
  4. Click Print.

To change the layout of these pages, click Edit... (see the View+Edit tab chapter).

Add a table of contents #

  1. On the Basic tab, choose Multiple Books and the books to print.
  2. On the Peripherals tab, tick Table of Contents.
  3. Type the Title, for example "Contents" in your language.
  4. Tick the book names to use (\toc1, \toc2, \toc3) and choose the Leaders.
  5. If Local Front Matter is ticked, check that the front matter contains \ztoc|main\* (the BASIC template has it).
  6. Click Print. If the status line asks you to rerun, click Print again.

Make a cover #

  1. Tick Local Front Matter (a cover needs it).
  2. Tick Create Cover Page.
  3. Click Cover Wizard..., go through the steps and click Finish.
  4. Click Print. The cover is saved as a separate PDF whose name ends with _cover.
  5. To fine-tune colours, borders or pictures, click Front Cover, Spine, Back Cover or Cover Spread and change the style on the Styles tab.

Add an existing PDF before or after the Scripture text #

  1. Tick Front Matter PDF(s) (or Back Matter PDF(s)).
  2. Click Select... and choose one or more PDF files.
  3. Click Print.

Put the copyright and picture credits at the end of the book #

  1. Tick Colophon at End of Publication.
  2. If the box is empty, click the reset button under the box to get the standard text.
  3. Tick Force Page Break Before Colophon if you want it on its own page.
  4. Click Print twice, so that the picture credits are correct.

Add your own variable #

  1. Click Add, type a name such as printedby, and click OK.
  2. Click the Value of the new row and type the text.
  3. On the View+Edit tab, put \zvar|printedby\* in the front matter where the text should appear.

Insert book group introductions from the INT book #

  1. In Paratext, give each section of the INT book an id, for example \periph New Testament Introduction|id="intnt".
  2. On the Peripherals tab, tick Use Peripheral Introductory Sections.
  3. Print a set of books that includes a book of that group (for example MAT for intnt).
↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 18.8 Variables and Values18.10 Common problems →

18.10 Common problems #

The cover is not created. Check that Local Front Matter and Create Cover Page are both ticked. The front matter must contain cover sections: run the Cover Wizard and click Finish to create them. The cover is in a separate PDF file (name ending in _cover), not in the main PDF.

Create Cover Page became unticked by itself. You unticked Local Front Matter. A cover cannot be made without it. Tick both again.

The Cover Wizard button is greyed out. Tick Create Cover Page first.

The Finish button in the Cover Wizard is greyed out. You must type a title in the front cover step, and be on the last (review) step.

My hand-made changes to the cover text disappeared. Finish in the Cover Wizard replaces the cover sections of the front matter. Make the changes again on the View+Edit tab after you use the wizard.

"Existing cover settings found" when I open the Cover Wizard. The configuration has cover styles or sections that the wizard did not make, or that were changed afterwards. To use the wizard, PTXprint must delete them. Click Cancel (keep my settings) to keep your cover and change it by hand.

The colophon disappeared after I turned on Local Front Matter. Ticking Local Front Matter unticks the colophon. Tick the colophon again if you want both. It is not unticked again unless you click Local Front Matter again.

The table of contents is empty or the page numbers are wrong. Click Print again (especially if Quick Run is ticked). If Local Front Matter is ticked, the front matter must contain \ztoc|main\*. Check that at least one of \toc1/\toc2/\toc3 is ticked and that the books have those markers in Paratext.

A book is missing from the table of contents. The book has no text for the ticked \toc markers. Add the \toc1 (or \toc2, \toc3) line to the book in Paratext, or tick another \toc option.

The picture credits in the colophon or front matter are wrong or empty. Click Print a second time. PTXprint needs a first run to find the page of each picture.

A variable prints as "". Click its Value in the Variables and Values table and type the text.

A variable I deleted came back. Rescan peripheral variables (and generating front matter) adds every variable used in the front matter. Remove the \zvar code from the front matter first, then delete the row.

There is a blank page before the Scripture text. PTXprint starts the Scripture text on a right-hand page. Tick Suppress Blank Page Before Scripture Text if you do not want this.

The maps are printed although I do not want them. Untick Include Maps.

Most of the settings on this tab are missing. You are using the Basic view. Change to the Regular or Full view.

18.11 Settings reference #

Peripherals #

Create Cover Page #

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views
Also: Create an outer Cover · Shown when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication”

Create a cover (back, spine and front) as a separate PDF file ending in _cover.pdf. Needs Local Front Matter. Use the Cover Wizard... to design it.

The cover pages are taken out of the main PDF. The cover text is kept in cover sections of the front matter, so unticking Local Front Matter unticks this too.

Cover Wizard... #

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views
Also: Generate Cover (Basic settings to create a cover) · Needs: “Create Cover Page” · Shown when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication”

Creating a cover from nothing takes a lot of effort. This tool enables you to create various kinds of covers which can easily be enhanced.

Leads you through 6 or 7 steps (page count and spine, pictures, background, front text, spine text, back cover, review) with a live preview. Finish writes the cover sections into the front matter (replacing earlier ones), sets the cover styles, ticks Local Front Matter if needed, and fills in the maintitle, subtitle, languagename and isbn variables. PTXprint asks before it deletes an older cover that the wizard did not make (or that was changed by hand). Cancel keeps everything as it was.

Shown when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication”

Click to edit the Sidebar properties on the Styles tab for the whole Cover Spread (the background behind the back, spine and front).

The bottom layer: the back, spine and front boxes are placed on top of it. Use it for a background colour or one picture across the whole cover.

Front Matter PDF(s) #

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views
Also: Enable import of front matter PDF(s) · Shown when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication”

One or more previously created PDF file(s) can be included BEFORE the scripture material being typeset. If more than one file is selected, then these will appear in alphabetical order.

If you are creating an electronic publication and want to add a fancy (colour) cover, then consider designing a cover using the online Canva.com tool.

The pages go before the local front matter too. Use it for pages made in another program. The pages should have the same page size as the publication.

Select... #

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views
Also: Select front matter PDF(s) to import · Needs: “Front Matter PDF(s)” · Shown when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication”

Hold the Ctrl key to choose several files. The names are shown next to the button, and the full paths when you hold the mouse over it. Several files are added in alphabetical order of their file names. To change the list, click the button again and choose all the files you want.

Table of Contents Title #

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views
Also: Enable table of contents · Shown when: “Table of Contents Title”, “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication”

This will automatically generate the Table of Contents for all the books included in the publication using one or more of the \toc1, \toc2 and \toc3 fields as specified. The \toc1, \toc2 and \toc3 choices are only applied when "Multiple Books" is set on the Basic tab.

NOTE: PTXprint typesets the text more than once to get the page numbers right, so printing takes longer. (With Quick Run on, click Print a second time.) If Local Front Matter is on, put \ztoc|main\* in the front matter where the ToC should appear.

Without Local Front Matter, PTXprint makes its own contents page with the Title. With it, the table appears where the front matter has \ztoc|main\*. See "Table of Contents" in this chapter.

Table of contents title #

Text box · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views
Needs: “Table of Contents Title” · Shown when: “Table of Contents Title”, “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication”

The heading for the Table of Contents (for example 'Contents' in your language). It can also be used in the front matter as \zvar|toctitle\*

Write it in the language of the publication. PTXprint uses it on its own contents page.

Checkbox (ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views

Select which of the \toc markers should be included in the generated Table of Contents.

Leaders – Style of leaders for table of contents #

Drop-down list · shown in: Regular and Full views
Choices: None | ...................... | . . . . . . . . . . . . . | - - - - - - - - - | ________________ · Needs: “Table of Contents Title” · Shown when: “Table of Contents Title”, “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication”

Leaders display dots or a line between the text and the page number. Select the style of leader you wish to apply.

None leaves the space empty. Leaders help the reader follow the line across a wide page.

Use Peripheral Introductory Sections #

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views
Shown when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication”

Check this option if the INT book contains peripheral divisions (sub-sections) which need to be inserted at the appropriate position between books. For example:
\periph Old Testament Introduction|id="intot"
\periph New Testament Introduction|id="intnt"
\periph Gospels Introduction|id="intgospels"

Uses \periph ids such as intot, intnt or intgospels (see the table in this chapter). A section is only printed if a book of its group is printed. Leave it unticked if your project has no INT book with such sections.

Local Front Matter #

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views
Also: Enable (local) front matter · Shown when: “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”, “Colophon at End of Publication”

PTXprint does not directly typeset the FRT book from Paratext. Instead, it uses a "local" PTXprint-specific copy of Paratext's FRT book which can be enhanced by additional codes which are described on the View+Edit tab's Information button.

Note: turning this on turns the Colophon off (you can turn it on again). A cover needs Local Front Matter.

Edited on the View+Edit tab. The first time, PTXprint creates a simple front matter if there is none. Your click to tick it unticks Colophon at End of Publication; your click to untick it ticks the colophon again and turns off Create Cover Page. The Cover Wizard ticks this box when you click Finish.

By default, the main body of scripture always starts on an odd (right-hand-side) page. PTXprint will automatically insert a pagebreak if needed to make this happen. If you wish to override this behavior, then check this option (to NOT insert a blank page after any front matter material).

Variables and Values #

Label · shown in: Basic, Regular and Full views
Shown when: “Local Front Matter”, “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Colophon at End of Publication”

This table lists the standard set of \zvar|variables\* which can be used as part of front matter and/or colophon. As these \zvar|variables\* are customizable, you can add your own as needed. For example, you may need the \zvar|maintitle\* in more than one language so you can add 'fr' or 'es' to create a new one:
\zvar|maintitlefr\* or you might want to add a custom variable such as:
\zvar|printedby\*

The values of these variables are saved with the config as they might vary from one publication to another.

Del #

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views
Also: Delete a peripheral variable · Shown when: “Local Front Matter”, “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Colophon at End of Publication”

Delete the currently selected variable(s).

Select several rows with Ctrl or Shift. A variable that the front matter still uses comes back at the next rescan.

Add #

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views
Also: Add a peripheral variable · Shown when: “Local Front Matter”, “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Colophon at End of Publication”

Add a new variable.

Adds the variable with an empty value. Use only letters, numbers and hyphens (no spaces), for example printedby or maintitlefr. Then type its value in the table, and use it in the front matter as \zvar|name\*. Nothing is added if the name already exists.

Colophon at End of Publication #

Colophon Text #

Label · shown in: Regular and Full views
Needs: “Colophon at End of Publication” · Hidden until: “Colophon at End of Publication” · Shown when: “Colophon at End of Publication”, “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”

Enter your Colophon text here - using standard USFM codes for formatting. You may want to use the reset button to start with a standard set.

You can use the following codes to automatically include special text using the following markers:
\zcopyright - copyright statement from the Basic tab
\zlicense - License text from the Basic tab
\zimagecopyrights - Automatically generated list of images, page numbers and attributions.
\zimagecopyrightsfr - as above, but use localized (fr = French) version (es, fr, hu, id, pt, ro available).

\b can be used to insert a blank line between markers if needed.

If using a Left-to-Right script for the colophon in a RTL publication you will need to add \beginL to force the colophon to render LTR. For example:
\pc \beginL \zcopyright
\pc \beginL \zlicense
\pc \beginL \zimagecopyrights

These special codes may also be used in other books such as the front matter book (FRT).

IMPORTANT: You will have to click Print a second time in order to get accurate Image Copyright Attribution.

Colophon text entry #

Text area · shown in: Regular and Full views
Needs: “Colophon at End of Publication” · Hidden until: “Colophon at End of Publication” · Shown when: “Colophon at End of Publication”, “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”

Note: There are several shortcuts you can use:
(c) --> © the copyright sign
(r) --> ® to denote registered trademarks
(tm) --> ™ to denote trademarks in general

Other special codes converted at print time:
use ~ for places where a non-breaking space is needed use // where a line break needs to be forced but :// used in URLs will still be preserved

Start each paragraph with a marker such as \pc (centred). \zcopyright, \zlicense and \zimagecopyrights insert the copyright, the licence and the picture credits. For a translated picture-credit list, add a language code, for example \zimagecopyrightsfr.

Clicking this button will reload the default Colophon text m... #

Button · shown in: Regular and Full views
Needs: “Colophon at End of Publication” · Hidden until: “Colophon at End of Publication” · Shown when: “Colophon at End of Publication”, “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”

Clicking this button will reload the default Colophon text markers which include the Copyright statement tag, the License statement tag, and the Illustration credits tag. Your current colophon text will be replaced.

The standard text is copyright, licence, a blank line and the picture credits. For a diglot it also includes the copyright of the second language. Your own colophon text is lost.

Force Page Break Before Colophon #

Checkbox (not ticked by default) · shown in: Regular and Full views
Needs: “Colophon at End of Publication” · Hidden until: “Colophon at End of Publication” · Shown when: “Colophon at End of Publication”, “Front Matter PDF(s)”, “Back Matter PDF(s)”, “Table of Contents Title”, “Local Front Matter”

Normally the colophon is inserted at the end of the last page of the last book. If this option is checked, then the colophon will appear at the bottom of a new page at the end of the publication.

In Diglot publications, the colophon always appears on its own page - regardless of this setting.

Without it, the colophon follows the last lines of the last book on the same page (if there is room).

19. Publications tab #

In this chapter
  1. 19.1 What this tab is for
  2. 19.2 The list of publications
  3. 19.3 The buttons
  4. 19.4 Printing the publications
  5. 19.5 Common tasks
  6. 19.6 Common problems
  7. 19.7 Settings reference

19.1 What this tab is for #

Use this tab to make several similar books from one project with the same design, without making a new configuration for each. For example: one PDF for each Gospel, or a New Testament and a separate book of Psalms, each with its own title.

A publication here means this configuration, printed with

  • its own list of books, and
  • its own values for some front matter variables (for example the main title and the subtitle).

All other settings (page size, fonts, layout, front matter, cover and so on) come from the current configuration. Make a list of publications, tick the ones you want, and click Print Selected. PTXprint makes one PDF for each ticked publication.

This tab is only shown in the Full view. (In the other views the Pub column in the variables table on the Peripherals tab is hidden too.)

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents19.2 The list of publications →

19.2 The list of publications #

The list has three columns:

  • Print – tick the publications to print. The checkbox in the column heading ticks or unticks all at once.
  • Publication ID / Field – on the first (bold) line of each publication, its name. Under it, the names of its fields (variables).
  • Books / Value – on the bold line, the books to print. Under it, the value of each field for this publication.

Click the small arrow beside a publication (or double-click its line) to show or hide its fields.

To change a value, click it, type the new text and press Enter. You can change:

  • the name of a publication (bold, second column). Each name must be different. The name is also used in the PDF file name, so keep it short and simple;
  • the books of a publication (bold, third column);
  • the value of each field.

You cannot change field names here. They come from the variables table on the Peripherals tab (see below).

The books #

Type the books as on the Basic tab, for example:

  • MRK – one book;
  • RUT JON – several books;
  • MAT-JHN – a range of books;
  • JHN 1-5 – some chapters of one book.

You can also type the name of a module file (a file that lists which parts of the text to print). If PTXprint cannot understand the books, the text turns red. Hold the mouse over it to see what is wrong.

The fields #

Each publication always has the fields maintitle and subtitle. To add more, tick Pub beside a variable in the Variables and Values table on the Peripherals tab. The variable is then added to every publication. Untick Pub to remove it again (not possible for maintitle and subtitle).

When you print a publication, PTXprint uses its values instead of the values on the Peripherals tab, for that one PDF only. The values on the Peripherals tab are not changed. The front matter (or the cover) must use the variables, for example \zvar|maintitle\* on the title page.

If the book has a cover with a spine, there is also a pagecount field: the number of pages of that publication. PTXprint uses it to work out the spine width for that publication's cover.

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 19.1 What this tab is for19.3 The buttons →

19.3 The buttons #

  • Add makes a new publication from the current settings.
  • Duplicate copies the highlighted publication, called "Copy of ...". This is the quickest way to make a set: duplicate, then change the name, books and title.
  • Delete removes the highlighted publication, after asking you.
  • Expand All / Collapse All show or hide the fields of all publications.
  • Print Selected prints every ticked publication.

The line at the bottom shows how many publications are ticked, and how many have books that PTXprint cannot understand.

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 19.2 The list of publications19.4 Printing the publications →

19.4 Printing the publications #

When you click Print Selected, PTXprint:

  1. saves the configuration (including the list of publications);
  2. checks the books of each ticked publication. If some are wrong, it asks whether to print the others and skip these;
  3. prints the publications in the background, several at the same time. Maximum parallel processes on the Advanced tab sets how many;
  4. opens the folder with the PDFs when all are finished.

Each PDF is named after the project, the configuration and the publication name. The PDFs are not shown in the PDF preview. Open them from the folder.

Print Selected is greyed out while the publications are printing.

Each configuration saves its own list of publications. When you switch configuration, the list shows the publications of that configuration (empty if it has none).

↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 19.3 The buttons19.5 Common tasks →

19.5 Common tasks #

Make one PDF for each Gospel #

  1. On the Peripherals tab, tick Local Front Matter and check that the title page uses \zvar|maintitle\* (the standard front matter does).
  2. On the Publications tab, click Add.
  3. Click the bold name and type Matthew. Click the books and type MAT.
  4. Open the publication, click the value of maintitle and type the title of Matthew in your language.
  5. Click Duplicate. Change the copy's name to Mark, its books to MRK, and its title.
  6. Do the same for Luke and John.
  7. Tick all four and click Print Selected.

Give each publication its own value for another variable #

  1. On the Peripherals tab, in the Variables and Values table, tick Pub beside the variable (for example isbn).
  2. On the Publications tab, open each publication and type its value.

Print only some of the publications #

  1. Untick all publications with the checkbox in the Print column heading.
  2. Tick the ones you want.
  3. Click Print Selected.

Remove a publication #

  1. Click the publication (or one of its fields).
  2. Click Delete, then confirm.
↑ Top of chapter⇑ Contents← 19.4 Printing the publications19.6 Common problems →

19.6 Common problems #

Print Selected is greyed out. No publication is ticked, or PTXprint is still printing the last set.

Duplicate and Delete are greyed out. Click a publication in the list first.

The books are shown in red. PTXprint cannot understand the list of books. Hold the mouse over the red text to see the problem. Use the 3-letter book codes, separated by spaces, for example GEN EXO.

"None of the selected publications can be printed". All ticked publications have no books or wrong books. Correct the books.

All the PDFs have the same title. The front matter does not use the variable, or uses a different one. Check that the title page contains \zvar|maintitle\* (see the View+Edit tab chapter), and that Local Front Matter is ticked on the Peripherals tab.

A variable is not in the publications. Tick Pub beside the variable on the Peripherals tab (the Pub column is only shown in the Full view).

"A publication called ... already exists". Each publication needs a different name.

The Publications tab is missing. Change the view level to Full.

My publications have gone. Check that you are using the right configuration. Each configuration keeps its own list.

20. Finishing tab #

In this chapter
  1. 20.1 What this tab is for
  2. 20.2 PDF Details
  3. 20.3 Booklet Pagination
  4. 20.4 Compare PDFs
  5. 20.5 Common tasks
